intro: Wet rooms have become one of the most popular bathroom upgrades across Greenton in recent years, and it's easy to understand why. They offer a clean, accessible, and genuinely luxurious alternative to a traditional shower enclosure or bath — and when done properly, they add real value to your home. Whether you're adapting a bathroom for accessibility reasons or simply want to make the most of your space, a well-installed wet room transforms how a bathroom looks and functions. In a town like Greenton, where homes range from characterful stone cottages to newer estate builds, getting the installation right means understanding the quirks of the property you're working with from day one.
localContext: Greenton's mix of older stone-built properties, period cottages, and modern estates means no two wet room installations are the same. Older stone-built homes and period cottages often come with solid concrete or suspended timber floors, uneven wall surfaces, and limited existing drainage infrastructure — all of which require careful survey work before tanking and waterproofing can begin. Modern estate properties tend to be more straightforward structurally, but bathroom sizes can be compact, which means clever design becomes even more important to make the space feel open rather than cramped. Greenton also sits in a moderately hard water area, which is worth factoring into your specification. Hard water causes limescale build-up on screens, tiles, and fittings, so many homeowners here opt for frameless glass screens, easy-clean tile finishes, and quality anti-limescale showerheads that reduce maintenance over time. Specifying the right materials from the start saves you cleaning headaches for years to come.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Greenton typically follows a clear sequence of stages, and understanding each one helps you know what to expect during the project. The first step is a thorough survey of the existing bathroom — your installer will assess the floor structure, wall construction, existing plumbing routes, and drainage options. This is where the differences between a period cottage and a modern new-build really show up, and where an experienced tradesperson earns their fee by spotting potential complications early. Once the survey is complete and a design is agreed, the existing bathroom is stripped back to the bare structure. For older Greenton properties, this sometimes reveals issues like damp patches, old pipe runs, or uneven subfloors that need addressing before anything else can proceed. The tanking system — a fully waterproof membrane applied to floors and walls — is then installed. This is the most critical stage of the entire job; inadequate tanking is the single biggest cause of wet room failures, so it should never be rushed or cut short. After tanking, the floor former or screed is laid to create the required fall toward the drain, ensuring water flows away properly rather than pooling. Tiling, screen fitting, shower valve installation, and final plumbing connections follow in sequence. A thorough final check confirms drainage performance and watertight integrity before the room is handed over.
pricing: In Greenton, most wet room installations fall somewhere between £6,000 and £12,500, depending on the complexity of the project and the specification chosen. Older stone-built properties and period cottages typically sit toward the higher end of that range due to the additional preparation work involved — remedying uneven floors, upgrading drainage, or dealing with solid walls all add time and materials. Modern estate homes with standard bathroom layouts tend to come in closer to the lower end. Tile choice, shower valve quality, glass screen specification, and whether you're upgrading the hot water supply to cope with the demand all influence the final figure. Always request a detailed written quote that separates labour from materials so you can compare accurately.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Greenton well makes a real practical difference on a project like this. Someone familiar with the area will understand the typical floor construction found in local period cottages, know the quirks of older plumbing layouts common in the town's stone-built homes, and have experience navigating the specific challenges that come up on East Sussex properties. They're also easier to get back should any snagging arise after completion. A wet room is a significant investment, and having someone with genuine local knowledge — rather than a travelling team unfamiliar with regional building styles — gives you a much more straightforward experience from first visit to final handover.

faqs.q: Will my older Greenton cottage floor be suitable for a wet room?
faqs.a: Many period cottages in Greenton have suspended timber floors, which can be made suitable but require additional work — typically installing a marine ply sub-base and a purpose-made wet room former before tanking begins. A solid concrete floor is generally more straightforward. A proper pre-installation survey will confirm what's needed and flag any structural concerns before work starts.

faqs.q: How do I manage limescale on a wet room in a moderately hard water area like Greenton?
faqs.a: Greenton's moderately hard water does mean limescale is a genuine consideration. The best approach is to specify easy-clean, low-grout tile formats, frameless glass screens rather than framed alternatives, and a quality showerhead with limescale-resistant nozzles. Some homeowners also fit an inline water softener or scale inhibitor on the shower feed, which significantly reduces build-up and keeps everything looking newer for longer.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Greenton?
faqs.a: For a standard bathroom conversion in a modern estate property, allow around five to eight working days. Older stone-built homes and period cottages in Greenton may need a day or two longer if preparatory work is required — remedying subfloors, rerouting pipes, or repairing damp patches. Your installer should give you a realistic programme once the initial survey is complete, so you can plan accordingly.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a property in Greenton?
faqs.a: Generally yes, particularly when the finish is high quality and the installation is sound. In Greenton's property market, a professionally installed wet room is seen as a genuine upgrade — especially in older stone-built homes or cottages where a stylish, accessible bathroom is less common. A poorly fitted wet room with tanking or drainage issues can have the opposite effect, which is why getting the installation right from the start matters so much.
